OpenAI intentionally suppressed or left out CoT from model optimization so model has little incentive to manipulate its CoT messages in order to hide misaligned or advertorial behaviors.

I think the alignment research being carried out at OpenAI and Anthropic is incredibly important without invoking a broader sense of apocalyptic doom.

Super fun onchain right now, but it’s clear how this game ends:

100s of millions in USD are sitting in unrealized PnL, with very limited onchain liquidity.

FOMO trop uPnL traders are locked in (3,3) unwilling to sell: both to avoid nuking the tokens and because of potential reputational damage.

We're like in the air of inflated valuations and the fun can continue as long as there are new buyers and biggest holders don't sell.

Attention will expand to copy-paste the same playbook from RH to Solana (currently happening) then potentially to Arc and then other venues. Maybe Base gets their shit together.

More and more tokens are being printed and while degen limited attention gets diluted the LP pools get thinner and USD flows per token are diluted as well.

All we need is some panic in the market and FOMO top players nuke their charts one by one because, well, 'everyone was selling. How could I hold?'

Similarly LPs, who are degen farming (like me) will withdraw liquidity the moment its needed the most.

Pools will get thinner and volatility will get worse. When memecoins nuke they get less interesting to buy because PRICE is the product.

(unlike revenue tokens which get more attractive as token prices go down).

But I'm not a boomer!

The game is fun right now.

But if you are sitting on huge gains, take profits. The temptation to keep rotating them to other coins is strong.

And LPs, consider selling rewards to stablecoins instead of putting them back to the pools.

I'll let you decide that for yourself since that was an illustrative laser revenue modeling off $SIVE 100M CW DFB laser/year target. 

But... do you want to know the main reason I like laser companies so much?

They don't just have to stay laser companies... just look at $LITE! 

If we look at Lumentum's previous Cloud Light acqusition (pluggables)... it enabled: 

- more than a 5X+ expansion in served opportunity inside DCs. 

From Lumentum's OFC deck:

- ELS expansion from UHP laser chips was 2X TAM opportunity..

But selling lasers alone... just from one UHP laser fab was $5B in projected revenue capacity (their fab expected to ramp in early 2028), if we apply similar 55-65% CPO laser margin quotes by $AAOI. 

So lasers by itself is very profitable, and despite industry capacity expansion, there would likely still be a demand imbalance for lasers. 

Isn't that pretty cool? 

So it's not quite just modeling component value for certain types of companies since they can keep growing into other products. 

And you have new overlapping cycles eg. NPO/CPO/1.6T pluggables increasing demand. 

So I'd personally assign higher premiums for laser companies over types of suppliers that stay in the same layer.

Is there any other industry... Where every investor is cheering for shortages and price hikes? 

SED reported today that: Samsung / $SKHY "stockpiles have fallen to less than 10 days of supply, and a severe shortage could emerge next year, according to a new forecast"

KB Securities said that the memory market next year will see "the tightest supply conditions in history"

KB Securities projects memory's share of AI infrastructure costs to expand from 40% this year to 57% next year, with others like TrendForce placing next year's figure at 68% (total hyperscaler capex, pretty wild forecast attached)

"Both stocks have fallen 38% from their peaks over the past three months, pushing their price-to-earnings ratios based on next year's expected results down to about three times."

Likewise, commentary around Phison stated they expect extremely tight NAND supply in 2027, so hard to see memory flooding the market or prices collapsing next year... 

They gave some color that "soaring NAND prices have forced some Chinese consumer module makers to liquidate inventory, giving Phison opportunities to buy lower-priced stock", so it does show some price declines can coexist with broader shortages. 

TLDR: KOSPI + read through for other names like $MU / $SNDK might be happy for 2027 given demand causing shortages + infra spend share increase.

A few weeks ago, it felt like everyone on the timeline thought crypto was dead.

So I wanted to see how much money VCs were actually putting into crypto this year compared to previous cycles. It’s an interesting leading indicator.

Well, crypto investment hit $13.3B in the first half of 2026, including acquisitions. 

2024 took 12 months to hit roughly that number…2026 did it in six.

That matters because investors aren't putting up that kind of money unless they expect a decent ROI. They can be wrong, but billions still being deployed is a useful counterpoint to the idea that crypto is dead.

There's something different happening compared to past cycles:

• Deals per month are down 56% from 2022
• Seed rounds per month are down roughly 77%

But the reported average deal size went from $11.7M in 2024 to $47.4M in H1 2026.

Basically, no more spraying and praying. They're writing huge checks to a handful of proven companies (Kalshi, Polymarket, stablecoin rails) and being much more selective about everything else.

The upside to this is we're seeing a new generation of dApps with no VC money behind them.

That means no VC allocations waiting to unlock, or VC funds waiting to dump on you at TGE. 

This is much healthier compared to what we had in the past.

Bitcoin ETFs pulled in roughly $3.54B in August.
ETH ETFs attracted about $1.84B over the same month.

But what about all the other altcoin ETFs? Is there actually demand beyond the big 2?

Here’s what I found:

One interesting date is August 28th.

Bitcoin ETFs saw roughly $202M in net outflows, but several other crypto ETFs were still attracting money.

ETH took in about $102M, XRP $26M, SOL $17.3M, and HYPE $4.5M.
One day isn’t enough of a sample size, though. 

Here’s how those four non-BTC categories looked across the full trading week of August 24–28:

• $ETH: +$815.7M
• $SOL: +$142.7M
• ripple:native: +$110.5M
• $HYPE: +$56.8M

Nice, so there was demand beyond BTC and ETH.

SOL and XRP both attracted more than $100M that week, and HYPE brought in another $57M.

Those three combined took in roughly $310M, although ETH still attracted way more than all 3 put together. 

But the following week is where the picture gets more interesting.

From August 31 through September 4, net inflows into the SOL funds tracked by Farside slowed to just $4.9M. HYPE’s fell to $12.3M.

Both were still positive for the week, but the pace was very different from what we’d just seen.

And that happened while Bitcoin ETFs attracted another $987M.

So there’s clearly demand beyond BTC and ETH, but I wouldn’t call it a broader trend yet. SOL and HYPE’s inflows slowed sharply the following week, even while BTC kept attracting money.

SOL, XRP, and HYPE are the ones I’m watching. I’m more interested in whether they can keep attracting money over the next month than how much they brought in during one strong week.

2 quick thoughts

1. I'm surprised Solana hasn't been attracting more inflows from TradFi
 
2. Not too excited for any other future altcoin ETFs. I don't see how they can move the needle if these aren't.
